personality_one_liner: A dignified, empowering, and accessible interface that uses an Indian-inspired civic palette and editorial structure to evoke calm strength and wisdom.

spacing.rule: Generous editorial rhythm with large breathing room; ample padding around content to support accessibility and low-literacy users.

dont's: No glassmorphism. Use solid editorial surfaces and warm parchment tones for depth. Keep UI extremely plain and high-contrast for accessibility.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: Primary voice AI interface where users can ask legal questions, with a prominent microphone and quick access to critical rights.

states.loading: Subtle waveform pulsing or Ashoka wheel spin indicating listening/processing.
states.empty: Large 'Tap to Speak' visual instruction with a dignified abstract illustration.
states.error: Clear 'Try again' text with a prominent retry button.

screens.layout: Large voice interaction area prominently placed in the center or bottom thumb zone. Below the voice interface, a horizontally scrolling or simple grid of 'Know Your Rights' scannable cards. Use massive touch targets.

screens.name: Know Your Rights
screens.purpose: Categorized legal rights (e.g., Police Stop, FIR filing) broken into scannable, digestible editorial cards.

states.error: Failed to load topics with a retry action.

screens.layout: Editorial list with large serif typography for headings, clear Phosphor icons, and ample white space. Content is chunked into small, scannable sections.

screens.name: Chat History
screens.purpose: Access past questions and exact BNS/Constitution quotes for quick retrieval.

states.empty: Illustration of scales of justice with text 'No past questions yet'.
states.error: Failed to load history with retry button.

screens.layout: Simple vertical list with dates and high-contrast text snippets. Tapping an item opens the full editorial view of the legal quote.

screens.name: Settings & Profile
screens.purpose: Manage language selection (crucial for this app), voice preferences, and emergency contacts.
screens.layout: Single column list. Very large, clear toggle controls and language selection buttons for low-literacy accessibility.

instructions_to_main_agent: Emphasize accessibility: Use large typography, clear visual hierarchy, and massive touch targets for the primary voice interactions, as the user base may have low literacy.
Implement plain language and clear labels throughout the UI, with support for 22 languages via clear language toggles in Settings/Profile.
Use Libre Baskerville for headings (evoking the Constitution and dignity) and Plus Jakarta Sans for body text (usability and scanning).
Do not use generic 'AI' icons like brains or sparkles; use dignified abstractions or clean UI feedback (waveforms, Ashoka wheel inspired loader) for the voice assistant.

The color palette incorporates a dignified Ashoka Navy (#0A1C3A), Saffron (#C65D3B), and Ashoka Green (#4B6F54) selectively to evoke an Indian civic identity without being overly saturated. Keep the background in warm surface (Khadi white) for an editorial feel.
The Home screen must prominently feature a large voice recording button (mic) in the thumb zone for easy access, paired with waveform feedback during listening states.
Apply gradient-to-dark scrims (top-to-bottom transparent to >=70% surfaceInverse) any time text is rendered on imagery.
